title: Public randomness services as one-time pads
instrument: round16/lib_padsweep.py dense_scan + A1 beam (beam_w=120, max_skip<=3, head=400), A1 score_norm scale

control.window_equivalence: sweep.py::_assert_window_equiv() re-proved the windowed beam/null bit-identical to lib_padsweep's before every run

nist_beacon_v1.window_note: end exclusive; 2013-11-14 is the first day the API would no longer serve completely (1206/1440), so the pad stops at the last fully fetched day rather than carrying fetch holes into the keystream

randomorg_archive.source: RANDOM.ORG Pregenerated File Archive - binary, one 1 MiB file of true random data per day, published daily since 2006-03-11

retrieval_measured_2026-08-19.direct_http_2013_file: https://archive.random.org/download?file=2013-12-01.bin -> HTTP 403 (subscription; only the newest day is free)

retrieval_measured_2026-08-19.how_this_lane_got_the_bytes: libtorrent 2.1.1 against random.org's own tracker, then every daily file checked against random.org's published MD5

extreme_value_check.note: AGENTS.md lesson 3 - a fixed bar is invalid at large N.

max_skip_robustness.why: lane P1 found A1's max_skip=3 underpowered on pads with constant byte runs (its control fell to 6/8 at ms=3, 60/60 at ms=8). This lane's pads were MEASURED for that structure (data/pad_run_structure.json) and are indistinguishable from iid; these re-runs confirm it empirically. Each re-scores offsets already counted above, at ms=8 with its own ms=8 null, so they add no coverage and are reported separately.
